_meta.description: Static precomputed npcId -> {race, gender, ethnicity?, lifeStage?} lookup plus cloud voice profiles, baked into the plugin. Generated offline by tools/generate_npc_voices.py from the Old School RuneScape Wiki (Infobox NPC and Infobox Monster pages; Monster races derive from page categories). Do not hand-edit; edit tools/overrides.json or tools/profiles.json and regenerate.
_meta.schema: npcs[id] = { race, gender, ethnicity?, lifeStage? }; symbols[id] = cache symbol, only for ids whose byId name another id shares
_meta.source: oldschool.runescape.wiki Infobox NPC (race/gender/leagueRegion/location) and Infobox Monster (race from page categories), cross-referenced by name against a full id dump for variant ids, gender corrected from RuneLite NpcID cache symbols, + curated tools/overrides.json; profiles from tools/profiles.json.

profiles._comment: Authoritative, curated character voice profiles for the cloud (Gemini 3.8) TTS backend. A profile is a delivery template (name, accent, accentDetail, style, pace, pitch, voiceRegion). The backend renders it, plus the line's chat-head emotion, into one style string sent in speech_metadata.style ('Speaking <language>. <gender>. [<pitch>.] Audio profile: <name>, a character in a medieval fantasy world. Accent: ... <accentDetail> Style: ... Pace: ... <emotion>.', plus a speed direction on Google AI Studio when Speaking Pace is not 100); the text sent to the model is the spoken line alone. accent must be a strong, explicit accent phrase naming its pronunciation ('Strong London English accent, British English pronunciation'), since Gemini 3.8 falls back to a generic default accent on a soft one; a delivery quirk (slurred, whispered) belongs in style, never in accent. style and pace are descriptive delivery prose. Optional 'pitch' leads the profile, right after the spoken language and the speaker's gender ('Very high-pitched, squeaky, thin little voice, far above a normal adult voice'); native library voices ignore pitch described later in the style, so pitch leads. Optional 'accentDetail' sits next to an accent and gives it its medieval colour in prose ('A rough, harsh British English, the hard edge of the outlaws of the Wilderness.'). Optional 'voiceRegion' sits next to an accent that has native speakers in tools/voice-regions.json. No meta-instructions ('word for word') and no square- or angle-bracket tags. This file is the SOURCE: tools/generate_npc_voices.py embeds it verbatim into src/main/resources/npc-voices.json under the top-level 'profiles' key. Edit here, then regenerate. Repetition across layers (depth in pitch and style, an accentDetail restating its accent, the generic human style under a bespoke one) is deliberate emphasis tuned by ear; do not tidy it (see docs/npc-voice-tooling.md, 'Repetition is deliberate'). This is a BRITISH medieval fantasy world: every character defaults to a British accent unless lore or trope says otherwise. Resolution combines every matching layer: default -> byRace[race] -> byEthnicity[ethnicity] -> every byCategory whose keyword matches the display name -> the child category for a child the table marks with lifeStage but whose name carries no child keyword -> byId[npcId]. 'style' accumulates across the matching layers, except that a layer with 'replaceStyle': true drops the less specific styles before its own; 'name', 'accent', 'pace', and 'pitch' take the most specific layer that sets them, and 'voiceRegion' and 'accentDetail' always come from the layer that set the winning accent. 'default' must be complete (all four fields); every other layer is sparse, contributing only the fields it sets. byId entries are per-NPC bespoke overrides keyed by the live NPC id (NPCComposition#getId), carrying only what is unique about that character.

default.name: Gielinor Commoner

default.accentDetail: Common British English, the plain, earthy speech of an ordinary medieval peasant or townsperson, not posh or refined.
default.style: A grounded medieval fantasy townsperson. Plain, sincere, and natural, with the easy warmth of someone going about their day.
default.pace: Steady and conversational, with natural pauses at the punctuation.

byEthnicity._comment: Accent layer keyed by an NPC's ethnicity (where they are from, baked per-NPC into npcs[id].ethnicity; defaulted from the wiki leagueRegion and corrected in overrides.json for foreigners). Applied only to the plain folk (Human / unknown race) so it tints them with local colour, while distinctive races (dwarf, elf, troll, goblin, undead, demon, wizard) keep their racial accent wherever they are. A keyword category (vampyre, ghost) or a bespoke byId entry can still override. Sparse and mostly accent-only, so it does not dilute the persona blend; a region may also set a style, and with 'replaceStyle': true (only the Wilderness) that style replaces the generic human one. The desert and far lands follow the real-world cultures they are based on; the central British kingdoms use distinct English regional accents for variety. NPCs with no single ethnicity keep the common British default.

Earnest, eager and wide open about how he feels, tipping into flustered babbling the moment the crab he loves comes up, and finding a wobbly courage when it counts.

16484.name: Crab
16484.style: A shy crab who cannot get a word out near the bass player she adores. Softly spoken and self-effacing, dreading being looked at, going quiet and tongue-tied whenever he is mentioned, and quietly certain of how she feels underneath it all.

16485.name: 'Crab'
16485.style: A Killer Gentoo Penguin working the beach in a crab costume, certain the disguise is flawless. Flat, formal and utterly deadpan, treating a shoreline of crabs as hostile territory and reporting the obvious as classified intelligence.
